chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, who said:

A man came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said, 'I do not know how to perform manual labor with my hands, nor do I know how to trade, and I am a laborer and needy.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Work, so carry [loads] upon your head, and become independent of the people. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had carried a stone upon his shoulder and placed it in a wall from his walls. And indeed, the stone is in its place, and it is not known how deep it is, except that it is there.'

key_terms.مُحَارَفٌ: A laborer or one who works with their hands

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq advise a needy man to do to achieve financial independence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (as) advises a laborer lacking specific trade skills to engage in manual labor, such as carrying loads, to achieve self-sufficiency (*istighna*) and avoid dependence on others. He grounds this practical advice in the Prophetic precedent of Muhammad (saww) personally carrying stones to build his own wall, highlighting the virtue of the Imams and Prophet engaging in humble physical work to maintain dignity and financial independence. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on active participation in livelihood generation as a form of worship and emulation of the Ahl al-Bayt.
